title: POV: You Save Your First $1,000 in 90 Days — Jake Earns $900 More and Has $0 When His Car Breaks
description:
How to save your first $1,000 in 90 days on a normal paycheck: six small moves, no raise, no side hustle. Same week, same $600 car repair: you pay it calmly, Jake puts it on a credit card.

In this POV story you earn $3,200 a month and still build a $1,000 starter emergency fund: a separate savings account at another bank, $50 sent automatically every payday ($300), cancelled subscriptions ($90), four unused things sold ($235), a 10-minute Sunday grocery plan ($300) and three no-spend weekends ($75). Jake earns $900 more but has nothing saved, so his $600 repair goes on a card at 22% and, at $25 a month, takes almost three years and about $800 to pay off.

short2.title: POV: Mia Spends $180 on a Costume She Wears Once… You Spend $12 🎃
short2.description: Halloween on a budget: NRF expects Americans to spend about $115 per person on Halloween this year. Mia buys a $180 costume she wears once. You build yours from your own closet plus a $12 prop, buy one bag of candy from your list, and get next year's decorations on November 1, when they're often half off or more.
